opex.heading: Operating Expenses
opex.text:
Lease Operating Expense (“LOE”): LOE includes costs incurred to maintain producing properties. Such costs include direct and

contract labor, repairs and maintenance, water hauling, compression, automobile, insurance, and materials and supplies expenses.

The increase in LOE was driven by the acquisitions of Maverick and Canvas. Specifically, the increase in LOE per Mcfe was

primarily related to a greater exposure to liquids production. Areas with higher liquids output tend to incur elevated operating costs,

although they also benefit from higher realized prices. In 2025 , the Company’s liquids production grew by 122% compared to 2024,

primarily driven by the acquisitions of Maverick and Canvas .

Production Taxes : Production taxes include severance and property taxes. Severance taxes are generally paid on produced natural

gas, NGLs and oil production at fixed rates established by federal, state, or local taxing authorities.

As of December 31, 2025 and 2024 , total borrowings were $3.0 billion and $1.7 billion , respectively. For the year ended

December 31, 2025 , the weighted average interest rate on borrowings was 7.61% compared to 7.37% for the year ended December 31,

compared to 83% as of December 31, 2024 .

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
The amount of income taxes recorded requires interpretations of complex rules and regulations of federal and state tax jurisdictions.

We recognize current tax expense based on estimated taxable income for the current period and the applicable statutory tax rates. We

routinely assess potential uncertain tax positions and, if required, estimate and establish accruals for such amounts. We have

recognized deferred tax assets and liabilities for temporary differences, operating losses and other tax carryforwards. In assessing the

need for a valuation allowance or adjustments to existing valuation allowances, we consider a variety of positive and negative

evidence, which may include a projection of income exclusive of existing timing differences. Our judgment regarding the realizability

of deferred tax assets is thus partially affected by estimates of future financial results.

Management monitors company-specific, natural gas and oil industry and worldwide economic factors and assesses the likelihood that

our net deferred tax assets will be utilized prior to their expiration. Refer to Note 4 in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
